title: Mimicking myocardial infarction: a subarachnoid haemorrhage case report
case_prompt: A 23-year-old man presented with sudden onset of severe frontal headache of 2 hours’ duration associated with nausea, vomiting, and chest heaviness. He had no significant past medical history, denied illicit drug use, but reported a 23–pack-year history of smoking. On examination, he was distressed but alert and oriented. Neck stiffness and dilated reactive pupils were noted; there were no focal neurologic deficits. His blood pressure was 178/103 mmHg, heart rate 87 bpm, respiratory rate 26/min, temperature 38.9 °C, and oxygen saturation 94% on room air. An ECG showed >2 mm of ST-segment elevation in leads V2 through V5. Initial high-sensitivity troponin was 1.48 mg/dL (normal <0.16 mg/dL). He was taken for percutaneous coronary intervention, which revealed normal coronary arteries with TIMI flow grade 3. A post-angiography ECG showed normal sinus rhythm with left ventricular hypertrophy. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated normal ventricular function without regional wall-motion abnormalities. Laboratory tests revealed a white-cell count of 17.9×10^3/µL with lymphocytosis, platelets of 123×10^3/µL, and a C-reactive protein level of 12 mg/L (normal <10 mg/L).
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Acute myocardial infarction was initially considered given ST-segment elevation and troponin rise — “ECG revealed ST segment elevation >2 mm in leads V2-V5, consistent with STEMI as the top of our differential diagnosis… Troponin levels were significantly elevated at 1.48 mg/dl” and was excluded after percutaneous coronary intervention showed “normal coronary arteries with thrombolysis in myocardial infarction (TIMI) flow grade of 3.”  
2. Neurogenic stunned myocardium from intracranial hemorrhage was considered as a cause of STE given the acute neurological presentation — “intracranial bleeding… can elicit sympathetic surges, impacting cardiac repolarization and potentially inducing STE on electrocardiograms” and “Neurogenic stunned myocardium is a recognized entity, characterized by transient cardiac dysfunction secondary to neurological insult, contributing to ST-segment elevation.”
